Liver tumor PDT
Photodynamic Therapy for Canine Liver Tumors
Principal Investigator
Bio Item
Joanne Tuohy, DVM, PhD, DACVS–Small Animal
, bio
Associate Professor, Surgical Oncology
tag:
Surgical Oncology
tag:
Oncology
tag:
Animal Cancer Care and Research Center
tag:
Small Animal Clinical Sciences
Contacts
Robyn Fox
, LVT
Clinical Trials Coordinator
Purpose
To evaluate a new treatment called photodynamic therapy (PDT) for dogs who have been diagnosed with liver tumors. The goal is to find out if PDT can be done safely, and see if it helps destroy the tumor cells in the liver. The long-term objective is to develop a minimally invasive way of treating liver tumors.
Background
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of liver cancer diagnosed in dogs. While current treatments like radiation and targeted chemotherapy are available, they unfortunately rarely eliminate the tumors completely. Surgical removal of the tumor and affected portion of the liver remains the standard of care option; however, not every patient is eligible for surgery.
To provide better options for pets, our research team is evaluating a groundbreaking new treatment called Photodynamic Therapy utilizing Light-Activatable Sustained-Exposure Ethanol Injection Technology—or LASEIT-PDT. This innovative technology has the potential to significantly advance how we treat canine liver cancer.
Eligibility
dogs recently diagnosed with a liver tumor
dogs whose families have elected surgical removal of the liver tumor
Exclusion
Presence of other life-threatening diseases
Non-resectable liver tumors
Study Design
Patients who have undergone a surgical workup will be deemed eligible for the trial based on CT scan and bloodwork.
Eligible dogs will undergo the PDT therapy under anesthesia, where a drug called verteporfin is injected into the liver tumor under CT guidance.
Dogs will be monitored in the ICU for two nights until standard surgical resection of the liver tumor on the second day after PDT therapy
Blood samples will be collected during the hospital stay
Compensation
Costs associated with diagnosing the liver tumor are not covered by the study. Once enrolled, the study covers the cost of PDT treatment, the recheck CT scans, hospital stay charge during the 2-day study period between PDT treatment and liver tumor removal surgery. The study also pays $2000 towards the cost of standard liver tumor removal surgery. The study does not cover costs associated with any complications from PDT treatment. Owners are responsible for their own travel costs.

UK-VCSR-2026-00013
Evaluating use of immune therapy in equine allergic reactions
Interventional
· Other
· Investigator: Dr Sally Gallop
Equine
Study overview
The study aims to assess effective of use of immune therapy in equine allergies compared to other therapies on the market. Collaborating veterinary practices will be requested to refer suitable participants, following discussion with horse's owner. Initial administration will be supervised by ESG staff, and collaborating veterinary practice staff will be trained in all study related procedure to deliver subsequent visits and collect required data.
Lay summary
Horses suffer from a wide range of allergies, which can impact their quality of life and limit their working ability. In recent years various treatments have been provided to reduce allergic reactions in horses. Once a blood based allergy test is conducted, selection of allergens is identified and immune therapy targeting these allergens can be developed and administered over period of weeks. We aim to assess if such therapy is better than other therapies on the market and it's cost effectiveness. Horses will be enrolled with owner permission and receive immune therapy over 12 weeks, followed up again at 4 months, 6 months, 8 months and 12 months.
Objectives
Primary objective
Assess effectiveness of immune therapy in equine allergies
Secondary objective(s)
Assess cost effectiveness of equine therapy compared to other treatments
Condition
equine allergies
Eligibility criteria
Inclusion
Horses who display allergic reactions (skin, airway etc.) aged 1 to 25
Exclusion
pregnant mares, lactating mares, horse under 1 year, horse over 25, horses who shown previous negative reaction to immune therapy
